checks.rpc-bench-tests: cargo test --locked --manifest-path rpc-bench/Cargo.toml --bin rpc-bench --test worker --test fairness

tasks.title: Split src/codegen.rs into a module tree with byte-identical output
tasks.deliverable: Mechanically split the 9k-line generator into src/codegen/{config,descriptors,naming,messages,parse,encode,json,text,reflection,native_stubs,tonic_stubs}.rs, declared from src/codegen.rs (lib.rs unchanged). No behavior or public API change.
accept: Regenerating every checked generated file and consumer fixture produces zero diff.
Public items reachable from pbrs::codegen are unchanged (compare `cargo doc` item lists before/after).
No submodule exceeds about 2,000 lines; later cards write exactly the named submodule files, so PK/GN/SV/H2/TC work stays disjoint.
tasks.notes: Land before PK-07, GN-02, SV-04, H2-10 and TC-03, which all edit codegen. Rebase over any open codegen PR first.

tasks.title: Split pbrs-grpc/src/client.rs into a client/ module tree
tasks.deliverable: Split pbrs-grpc/src/client.rs into client/{channel,pool,call,unary,streaming,retry,config_glue}.rs, declared from client.rs (lib.rs unchanged), without behavior change.
accept: All native test suites pass unchanged; no public API change.
Splits on top of the landed retry work (MX-00); never splits underneath unmerged work.

tasks.title: Split pbrs-grpc/src/server.rs into a server/ module tree
tasks.deliverable: Split pbrs-grpc/src/server.rs into server/{accept,connection,dispatch,router,rpc,drain}.rs, declared from server.rs (lib.rs unchanged), without behavior change.
accept: All native test suites and interop pass unchanged; no public API change.
Each submodule has one owner lane (SV, H2, RX) recorded in the plan's ownership table.

tasks.title: Repair tonic comparator fairness and retract unverified transport claims
tasks.deliverable: Make the tonic peer in rpc-bench comparable: set TCP_NODELAY on accepted sockets (tonic ignores the builder setting under serve_with_incoming), match stream/connection windows, max frame size, adaptive-window policy and concurrent-stream limits to the native peer, and run client and servers in separate processes. Verify socket options with getsockopt on both ends and record them. Rerun the historical transport cells and correct docs.
accept: Result JSON records observed TCP_NODELAY, windows, frame size and runtime threads per endpoint; the harness refuses to print a comparison when they differ.
A regression test fails if a tonic accepted socket lacks TCP_NODELAY.
docs/benchmarks.md labels the old tonic latency/QPS table superseded (with its commit) and removes the unproven Tower-buffer causal claim; new numbers are labeled dev-loop, not leadership.

tasks.title: Define the category scoreboard and record current standing
tasks.deliverable: Create the machine-readable scoreboard: category IDs from the plan, metric definitions and direction, comparator set with pinned versions, corpora/scenarios, dev-loop versus claim-grade win rules, and an initial standing table (win/tie/loss/unmeasured/invalid) with evidence links.
accept: Every category in the plan's scoreboard section appears exactly once with an owner lane.
Every existing performance statement in docs/benchmarks.md is mapped to a category and marked valid, unqualified or invalid (the SB-01 tonic cells start invalid).
No category is marked a claim-grade win without evidence meeting docs/benchmark-contract.md; dev-loop wins are labeled as such.

tasks.title: Build the deterministic dev-loop measurement harness
tasks.deliverable: Add bench/devloop (excluded standalone crate) and scripts/devloop.sh. For codec operations and loopback RPC shapes, report instructions retired (Linux perf counters when available, otherwise cachegrind/callgrind), exact heap allocations and bytes via a counting GlobalAlloc, syscalls per RPC when strace/perf is available, and wall time as a secondary metric. Emit versioned JSON and support --baseline comparison with thresholds.
accept: Repeat runs on one host vary by under 1% in instructions for codec cells and under 3% for RPC cells; observed variance is recorded in the README.
Allocation counts are exact and identical across repeats.
Missing external tools produce not_run for that metric, never a pass; no new crates.io dependency without review.
Comparators: prost and protobuf v4 for codec cells, tonic (SB-01 settings) for RPC cells.
tasks.notes: Cargo.toml edit is limited to adding bench/devloop to the workspace exclude list.

tasks.title: Add a CI performance-regression lane on dev-loop metrics
tasks.deliverable: Add a non-blocking Linux workflow that builds base and head in one job, runs the dev-loop suite for both, uploads JSON, and writes a delta summary. SB-20 later decides gating thresholds from the observed noise.
accept: Runs on PRs touching src/, pbrs-grpc/src/, protobuf-tonic/src/ or bench/devloop/; finishes under 20 minutes.
Summary lists per-cell instruction and allocation deltas; missing tools are reported as not_run.
Each run retains its JSON so SB-20 can compute noise across at least 30 runs.

tasks.title: Add realistic corpora and holdout schemas
tasks.deliverable: Add pinned, license-checked schemas and deterministic payload generators for OpenTelemetry OTLP (traces, metrics, logs), Envoy xDS resources (Cluster, ClusterLoadAssignment, RouteConfiguration with Any), googleapis samples, the historical google_message1/google_message2 datasets, and grpc.testing benchmark messages. Record primary versus holdout classification.
accept: Each corpus records upstream repository, commit and license; generated payloads are deterministic from a seed.
Primary and holdout sets are frozen in bench/scoreboard/categories.json before any optimization uses them.
Payload sizes span tiny (<64 B), typical (64 B-4 KiB), large (64 KiB-1 MiB) and huge (8-64 MiB).

tasks.title: Add C++ protobuf and upb C codec peers
tasks.deliverable: Build pinned C++ protobuf (arena and non-arena) and upb C harnesses from checksummed sources under bench/xlang, driven by the same corpora and emitting the dev-loop/claim JSON schema.
accept: Wire bytes or semantic equality are verified per cell before timing.
Peers that fail to build are not_run, never omitted; build steps are scripted and pinned.
These are test tools only and never enter a shipping dependency graph.

tasks.title: Add Go protobuf, vtprotobuf and hyperpb codec peers
tasks.deliverable: Add pinned Go harnesses for google.golang.org/protobuf, vtprotobuf generated fast paths and Buf's hyperpb dynamic parser, on the same corpora and JSON schema.
accept: Pinned module versions and go.sum are recorded; builds are offline-reproducible after fetch.
hyperpb is compared only in the dynamic-parse category (A12) and generated Go code in the typed categories.

tasks.title: Refresh Rust codec peers and use generated schemas
tasks.deliverable: Update prost, buffa (owned, eager view and lazy view as separate columns) and Google's runtime (google-protobuf 0.36.x, keeping protobuf 4.35.1 as the historical column) to pinned releases, add quick-protobuf where schemas allow, and ensure every scoreboard cell uses generated (not handwritten) pbrs types.
accept: Handwritten testdata types are excluded from scoreboard cells or labeled diagnostic; every cell performs equivalent work across codecs (BM-03 semantics: fresh, cached and mutated encode, parse-only versus parse-and-touch with output equivalence).
Peer versions and lockfile hashes are recorded in results; cross-codec equivalence checks run before timing.

tasks.title: Build the codegen comparator matrix
tasks.deliverable: Extend the CG-19 harness with prost-build plus tonic-build, protobuf v4 rust_out and buffa-build generators on the seeded 6/100/1,000-message corpora and the realistic corpora (OTLP, Envoy/xDS, googleapis subset). Measure generation time and RSS, generated bytes, clean and incremental cargo check, release build time and RSS, and binary size.
accept: Each generator produces a consumer doing equivalent work (construct, serialize, parse) for every message.
Randomized order across at least five repeats per cell; uncertainty reported; losses listed.
Service stubs are compared separately (pbrs native, pbrs tonic, tonic-build).

tasks.title: Honor official QPS scenario thread controls and run official scenarios
tasks.deliverable: Map async_server_threads/async_client_threads to explicit runtime worker counts instead of rejecting them, keep SYNC client/server types explicitly unsupported, and run every bundled official scenario end-to-end with the pinned C++ qps_json_driver in native/native, native/C++ and native/Go worker pairings.
accept: Meets the open acceptance criteria of legacy BM-08, BM-09, BM-10 and BM-11 (read those cards first); no requested control is silently ignored: honored controls are echoed in results, unsupported ones fail before bind.

The seven protobuf_* scenarios in rpc-bench/scenarios/official.json (unary ping-pong empty/1kb/64kb, streaming ping-pong empty/1kb, unary_qps_unconstrained_100rpcs, unary_poisson_5000qps) complete for native/native and native/C++ pairs; only the SYNC go_* aliases may stay unsupported, with a reason.
Results retain the driver's ScenarioResult JSON and worker logs and are labeled diagnostic (mostly closed-loop, 5 s warmup/30 s runs), not claim-grade; SB-21 creates the contract-compliant variants.

tasks.title: Build the cross-stack client/server matrix harness
tasks.deliverable: Create a grpc_bench-style matrix: each server under test pinned to 1/2/4 CPUs via cpusets or cgroups, driven by one independent pinned load generator (official C++ qps client or pinned ghz) in open-loop mode, and each client under test driven against one fixed reference server. Required peers: pbrs-grpc, tonic, grpc-go and grpc-c++. SB-18 adds optional peers and SB-19 adds the extended cells.
accept: Server cells report sustained success QPS at a p99 SLO, CPU per RPC, RSS and latency percentiles; client cells report client CPU per RPC at matched offered load with verified server headroom.
Peer builds are pinned and scripted; a required peer that cannot run fails the card instead of being reported not_run.
Payloads: empty, 1 KiB, 64 KiB; shapes: unary, server stream, bidi ping-pong; TLS off and on.

tasks.title: Measure connection scale, memory per connection and handshake rate
tasks.deliverable: Add scenarios for 1k/10k/100k idle connections (RSS per connection), active-stream memory, TLS handshakes per second per core, and connection-storm accept rate, for pbrs-grpc and the SB-11 peers.
accept: File-descriptor and sysctl limits are recorded; a run that hits an OS limit is marked invalid, not a loss.
Memory per connection is derived from RSS deltas with at least three repeats.

tasks.title: Attribute copies in large-payload and streaming paths
tasks.deliverable: Implement Phase 0 of the zero-copy plan: 1-64 MiB unary and streamed bytes/packed payloads, per-path copy counters behind a bench-only feature, flamegraphs, and baseline numbers for pbrs-grpc, tonic+prost (Bytes fields) and grpc-go.
accept: Every user-space copy on inbound and outbound paths is counted and attributed to a source location.
Baselines are recorded before any PK-09/10/11 change is eligible to merge.

tasks.title: Publish the profiling kit and perf-PR evidence template
tasks.deliverable: Document and script flamegraph capture (perf/dtrace/samply if already installed), allocation profiling via the counting allocator, and a pull-request evidence template: hypothesis, dev-loop before/after JSON, flamegraph links, correctness checks run, and rollback criterion.
accept: A worker can profile any codec or RPC cell with one documented command.
The template is referenced from the plan's worker protocol and used by every PK/CL/SV/H2 card.

tasks.title: Run claim-grade codec and codegen campaigns
tasks.deliverable: Operator task: on dedicated Linux x86_64 and arm64 hosts with docs/benchmark-contract.md section 8 controls, run the frozen primary and holdout codec (A) and codegen (B) cells against every pinned comparator with section 6 statistics and the section 7.2 thresholds.
accept: Raw artifacts, host inventory, sysctls, toolchains and peer versions are retained for every cell.
Every cell reports a 95% interval; losses are published beside wins.

tasks.title: Publish a generated scoreboard with raw artifacts
tasks.deliverable: Generate docs/scoreboard.md from results JSON (dev-loop and claim-grade tiers kept separate), link raw artifacts, show losses and not_run cells, and document the update procedure.
accept: The page is reproducible from committed JSON by one script; hand edits fail a check.
Headline wording follows docs/benchmark-contract.md section 10.2: named matrix only, no universal claim.

tasks.title: Rank codec bottlenecks with dev-loop evidence
tasks.deliverable: Profile fresh, cached and mutated encode, owned decode, parse-and-touch, merge, size and retained memory across primary and holdout corpora. Attribute instructions, allocations, copies and branch/cache behavior; nominate one measurable hypothesis per PK card and re-scope cards whose premise is disproved.
accept: Each nominated hypothesis cites dev-loop JSON and a flamegraph, names its target cells and a rollback criterion.
Cards whose hypothesis is disproved are re-scoped in tasks.json with the evidence, not implemented blindly.
tasks.notes: Executes OP-01 on dev-loop evidence instead of waiting for BM-13 dedicated hosts; claim-grade confirmation stays with SB-15.

tasks.title: Decide how to separate build-time code from the runtime
tasks.deliverable: Decide between cargo features (codegen, reflect, json, text) and a separate build crate so that runtime consumers stop compiling the generator, descriptor pool, JSON and text modules. Record compile-time and binary-size impact estimates, semver impact and the maintainer's small-cohesive-release preference.
accept: Decision record lists the chosen option, rejected options, migration for existing build.rs users and release impact.
Any new crate name is an explicit maintainer decision, not assumed.

tasks.title: Implement the runtime/build-time split
tasks.deliverable: Implement the PK-02 decision so a runtime-only dependency compiles without generator, reflection, JSON or text code unless requested; keep the default experience source-compatible.
accept: A runtime-only consumer builds with the documented feature set and measurably less clean-check time on the 100-message corpus (SB-09 cell).
Default-feature users see no API or behavior change; all existing tests and conformance pass.

tasks.title: Add SWAR/SIMD varint and tag decoding
tasks.deliverable: Replace the scalar varint and packed-varint validation loops with a portable SWAR fast path plus optional std::arch (SSE/AVX2, NEON) paths selected at compile or run time, preserving overflow, overlong and truncation semantics.
accept: Differential fuzzing against the scalar decoder finds no divergence over at least 1e9 inputs.
Dev-loop instructions improve on packed_256, unpacked_256 and tags_32 cells without regressing tiny-message cells by more than 1%.
Big-endian and 32-bit behavior is covered by Miri or cross tests.

tasks.title: Design the hybrid table-driven parser
tasks.deliverable: Design compact static per-message field tables (tag to handler, field kind, slot accessor, presence) plus a shared generic parse loop, keeping inline specialized parsing for small hot messages. Specify selection heuristics, code-size budget, unsafe invariants and how the same tables can later serve size/encode and the UK kernel.
accept: Design names the dispatch technique (e.g. tag-indexed jump table with fallback), unsafe boundaries and Miri plan.
Predicts effects on parse speed and generated code size, with the SB-09 cells used to judge them.
Keeps table formats compatible with the UK-02 kernel design where one exists; UK-18 owns later convergence, so this card does not wait for it.

tasks.title: Implement the table-driven parse engine in the runtime
tasks.deliverable: Implement the generic parse loop and per-kind handlers from PK-05 in the runtime, with unknown-field preservation, depth limits, UTF-8 rules per edition and lazy-field semantics identical to generated inline parsing.
accept: A differential test parses every conformance and corpus payload through both engines and compares messages and errors.
Miri passes on the engine's unit tests; unsafe blocks carry SAFETY comments.

tasks.title: Emit parse tables and auto-select parse strategy in codegen
tasks.deliverable: Generate the PK-05 tables for every message and choose inline or table parsing per message via the approved heuristic, with a Config/plugin override (parse_strategy = inline | table | auto).
accept: Conformance, google_shared and all generated-type tests pass under each strategy.
On SB-09 cells, table or auto mode reduces generated bytes and clean-check time; on dev-loop cells auto mode regresses no primary codec cell by more than 2%.

tasks.title: Use tables for cold size/encode paths
tasks.deliverable: Drive size computation and encoding of cold, wide or rarely populated fields from the same tables, keeping hot fields specialized, to cut generated code without slowing hot encode.
accept: Byte-identical encoded output across all corpora versus the current encoder.
Generated bytes and release build time fall on SB-09 cells; primary encode cells regress no more than 2%.

tasks.title: Add Bytes-owning parse and shared large-field backing
tasks.deliverable: Implement zero-copy plan phases 1a/1b: FrameReader reserves the known frame length; add Parse::parse_bytes(Bytes)/merge_from_bytes that retains shared backing for strings/bytes above a threshold; ProtoBytes gains a shared representation while keeping &[u8] accessors.
accept: SB-13 copy counters show one fewer inbound copy for large bytes fields; small-message cells do not regress beyond 1%.
Retained-memory tests show a small field cannot pin a large frame (threshold enforced).

tasks.title: Parse segmented DATA frames without coalescing
tasks.deliverable: Implement zero-copy plan phase 3: a Buf-chain cursor with a small slop buffer for tags/lengths that straddle chunks (EpsCopyInputStream style), rope-backed large bytes with a chunks() accessor, and lazy flattening for &[u8] accessors.
accept: Fuzzed chunk boundaries (every split point on corpus payloads) parse identically to contiguous input.
SB-13 shows no frame-join copy for multi-chunk large messages.

tasks.title: Encode shared segments and send scatter-gather
tasks.deliverable: Implement zero-copy plan phase 2: WireOut::put_shared (default put_slice) and a segmented sink yielding Vec<Bytes>, so retained large fields are sent without copying into the frame buffer.
accept: SB-13 shows the outbound copy removed for shared fields; gzip and TLS paths remain correct.
Frame boundaries and 5-byte prefixes are byte-identical to the contiguous encoder.

tasks.title: Experiment with per-request arena allocation
tasks.deliverable: Prototype an opt-in bump arena for owned messages parsed per RPC (no individual frees; drop resets the arena) and measure allocation counts, parse time and teardown cost against the global allocator with mimalloc/jemalloc/system.
accept: Decision record adopts or rejects with dev-loop evidence; rejection is a valid outcome.
If adopted, the design keeps the owned API safe (no dangling views) and is covered by Miri.

tasks.title: Decide the borrowed-view model
tasks.deliverable: Decide the public borrowed-view model: lifetime-bound FooView<'a> over &[u8], Bytes-leased views, or both; eager versus lazy nested views; accessor parity with the owned API; retained-memory policy.
accept: Decision record includes API sketches, retained-memory trade-offs measured on PK-09's Bytes backing, and the buffa eager/lazy comparison rules.
Maintainer approval before PK-20.

tasks.title: Reuse canonical packed payloads and speed large packed encode
tasks.deliverable: Record canonicality during packed-varint validation so the first encode can reuse the payload, and close the recorded 5 MiB packed-fixed encode gap versus upb.
accept: No overlong or non-canonical input is ever re-emitted unchanged (recommended conformance still passes).
Packed cold-encode and 1-5 MiB packed-fixed cells improve on dev-loop evidence.

tasks.title: Tune medium-string ownership thresholds
tasks.deliverable: Compare payload-only Arc, shared-parent window and owned storage for 24-200 byte strings under matched parse, touch and encode, and choose thresholds that close the name_80 loss without pinning large frames.
accept: name_80 and neighboring cells win or tie prost and v4 on dev-loop evidence.
Retained-memory test proves a short field does not pin a large parent frame.

tasks.title: Stream JSON encode and decode, including every well-known type
tasks.deliverable: Replace serde_json::Value construction and binary-to-dynamic fallbacks with streaming field-wise JSON writers and readers for all messages and every well-known type (Any, Struct, Value, ListValue, FieldMask included), preserving official protobuf JSON semantics.
accept: JSON conformance stays at zero unexpected failures.
JSON encode/decode cells beat C++ and Go protojson (SB-06/07 peers) on dev-loop evidence for OTLP and TAT corpora.

tasks.title: Adopt a hybrid map representation
tasks.deliverable: Keep append/last-wins parsing for small maps and switch to an indexed representation above a measured size so lookup, unique length and size computation stay fast on large maps.
accept: Duplicate-key semantics, iteration and encode order rules are unchanged (differential fixtures).
map_64 and larger map cells improve for parse-and-touch without regressing map_8.

tasks.title: Make dynamic-message parsing the fastest in class
tasks.deliverable: Compile descriptor-derived parse tables at runtime for DynamicMessage (hyperpb-style), reusing the PK-06 engine, with optional profile-guided field layout.
accept: Dynamic parse cells beat hyperpb and upb reflection on SB-07/SB-06 evidence for OTLP and Envoy corpora.
Dynamic JSON/text and conformance behavior unchanged.

tasks.title: Speed merge, clone and size, and publish PGO guidance
tasks.deliverable: Implement direct field-wise merge (no serialize/reparse), cheap clone of lazy fields, and cached size reuse; document and measure PGO/BOLT for downstream binaries.
accept: Merge semantics match conformance and differential fixtures.
Merge, clone and size cells improve on dev-loop evidence; PGO guidance includes measured gains and build-time cost.

tasks.title: Attribute downstream compile-time costs
tasks.deliverable: Use cargo --timings, rustc -Z self-profile (nightly, measurement only) and cargo llvm-lines if already available to attribute clean-check and release-build time on the 100/1,000-message corpora to generated constructs (trait impls, monomorphized generics, macros, descriptor embedding, always-built runtime modules).
accept: Ranked table of the top cost sources with measured share of check and build time.
Each GN/PK code-size card cites a row of this table.

tasks.title: Shrink generated code
tasks.deliverable: Move per-field generated logic into shared generic runtime helpers, collapse redundant owned/view/mut impls, mark cold paths, and remove per-message duplication identified by GN-01.
accept: Generated bytes, clean check and release build time fall on SB-09 cells; target: beat prost-build and the upb reference on B4 and B6.
No primary codec cell regresses by more than 2% on dev-loop evidence; generated public API unchanged.

tasks.title: Make descriptor embedding optional and shared
tasks.deliverable: Allow reflection-free generation, deduplicate embedded descriptor bytes across files, and load descriptors lazily when reflection is enabled.
accept: Reflection-free consumers compile and run all non-reflection tests; reflection users see no change.
Binary size and check time fall on SB-09 cells.

tasks.title: Make the generator itself the fastest
tasks.deliverable: Profile generation on 1,000-message and realistic corpora; remove quadratic lookups, allocate less, and emit files in parallel where deterministic.
accept: Output stays byte-identical and deterministic.
Generation time and RSS beat prost-build and protoc --rust_out on SB-09 cells (excluding protoc descriptor parsing unless the pure-Rust frontend is used).

tasks.title: Decide the pure-Rust .proto frontend route
tasks.deliverable: Choose between contributing Editions 2023/2024 grammar, import option, export/local and feature resolution to an existing Rust frontend (protox) upstream, or an in-repo frontend. Use docs/rust-frontend.md as the starting audit.
accept: Decision covers license, MSRV, transitive graph, maintenance ownership, upstream acceptance risk and schedule.
Maintainer approves before GN-06 starts.

tasks.title: Implement the frontend lexer and parser for proto2 and proto3
tasks.deliverable: Implement (upstream or in-repo per GN-05) the lexer and parser for proto2 and proto3 with spans and protoc-equivalent diagnostics.
accept: Every proto2/proto3 file in the GN-08 corpus parses, and every rejected fixture fails, as with pinned protoc (frontend-diff parse mode).
Fuzzing the parser for 1 CPU-hour finds no panic.

tasks.title: Implement frontend import and name resolution
tasks.deliverable: Resolve imports (public, weak, option), packages, nested names, extensions and cross-file references into descriptors.
accept: Descriptors for the corpus match pinned protoc for names, types and import graphs (frontend-diff link mode); options and source info follow in GN-07b.

tasks.title: Build the pinned frontend differential corpus and harness
tasks.deliverable: Add a pinned corpus (protobuf unittest protos, googleapis, Envoy data-plane-api, OpenTelemetry, grpc-proto, Edition 2024 fixtures) and scripts/frontend-diff.sh, which records pinned-protoc descriptor output and compares a frontend in parse, link and full modes.
accept: Corpus pins record upstream commits and licenses; the protoc baseline is reproducible.
The harness runs with no frontend present (baseline only) so later cards can adopt it immediately.

tasks.title: Prove Rust-only packaged consumers
tasks.deliverable: Build fresh packaged consumers (messages, native gRPC, tonic stubs) from .proto sources with no protoc and no C/C++ compiler on PATH, on Linux and macOS.
accept: CI job hides protoc and cc and still builds and runs all three quickstarts.
README support matrix updated with the Rust-only profile.

tasks.title: Inventory the official rust_out kernel ABI and its gaps
tasks.deliverable: Generate protoc --rust_out kernel=upb output at the pinned v35.1 regression baseline and at the current google-protobuf release line (v36.x) for every upstream Rust test proto and the SB-05 corpora, compile it against pbrs as the runtime crate, and produce a machine-readable list of every __internal::runtime item gencode uses, which exist, which are stubs (null/panic/constant) and which are missing, plus the compile-error count.
accept: docs/evidence/rust-out-abi.json lists each item with status implemented/stub/missing and the gencode sites that use it.
The known stubs are captured: enum mini tables, extension registry and MiniTableExtension, raw view interop, message_eq, debug_string, unknown-field retention in the generic parser.
A script regenerates the inventory from a pinned protoc so later cards can show the gap shrinking.

tasks.title: Decide the upb-in-Rust kernel architecture
tasks.deliverable: Write the kernel design: MiniTable binary layout compatible with upb mini descriptors, a fusing bump arena, message memory layout (hasbits, oneof case, field offsets), a table-driven decoder with tag-dispatch fast paths, a single-pass encoder, the extension registry, maps, unknown fields, and whether the plugin path shares these primitives. Place it relative to Google's stated direction (a Rust rewrite of upb, not another parser) and the grpc-rust dependency on protobuf 4.x.
accept: Design names crate placement (inside pbrs or a separate kernel crate, maintainer decision), unsafe boundaries, Miri/fuzz strategy, and performance targets per UK-13.
Lists which upstream upb tests are black-box portable and which are C-internal.
Maintainer signs off before UK-03 through UK-10 start.

tasks.title: Implement a fusing bump arena
tasks.deliverable: Implement the arena from UK-02: chunked bump allocation, fuse (union-find lifetime sharing), drop of Rust-owned payloads, alignment, and size accounting; replace the Rc<RefCell<Vec<Box<..>>>> stand-in behind the same ABI.
accept: Miri (strict provenance) passes the arena tests; fuse cycles and cross-thread send rules are tested.
rust_out_person and rust_out_shared still pass; allocation counts drop on the dev-loop rust_out cells.

tasks.title: Complete MiniDescriptor decoding and linking
tasks.deliverable: Decode upb mini descriptors for messages, enums and extensions into MiniTables, including field modes, packed/presence flags, closed-enum tables and sub-table linking; build_enum_mini_table and link_mini_table must stop being stubs.
accept: Unit tests decode mini descriptors extracted from pinned gencode for every upstream test proto and compare field-by-field with upb's decoded tables (dumped once by a C harness under bench/xlang).
Closed enums reject unknown values per upb semantics.

tasks.title: Adopt MiniTable-native message layout
tasks.deliverable: Replace boxed MsgData slot/presence vectors with contiguous arena-allocated messages laid out per MiniTable (hasbits, oneof case words, inline scalars, pointers for strings/sub-messages/arrays/maps).
accept: All accessor ABI entry points operate on the new layout; rust_out_shared passes.
Size of a populated TestAllTypes message and allocation count per parse are reported before/after.

tasks.title: Implement the fast table-driven decoder
tasks.deliverable: Implement decode over MiniTables with tag-dispatch fast paths (fasttable equivalent), unknown-field retention, decode options (check-required, alias strings to input, depth limit), groups and packed/unpacked leniency.
accept: Unit tests cover every field mode, and a differential test decodes all conformance and corpus payloads through the new decoder and the plugin parser with identical results and errors.
rust_out_shared passes; full conformance (UK-12) and differential fuzzing against upb C (UK-15) qualify it later.

tasks.title: Implement a single-pass encoder and exact size
tasks.deliverable: Encode without temporary Vecs for nested messages, packed fields and map entries (reverse encoding or cached sizes), provide a non-allocating serialized size, deterministic mode, and direct encode into caller buffers with a reserved gRPC prefix.
accept: Byte-identical output to upb C on all corpora in deterministic mode.
Encode and size cells on rust_out gencode improve on dev-loop evidence; no temporary allocation remains on the encode path.

tasks.title: Implement extensions for the official path
tasks.deliverable: Implement MiniTableExtension, extension registries, ExtensionSub and generated typed extension accessors expected by rust_out gencode; coordinate with CG-14b for the plugin path.
accept: Upstream extensions_test.rs (and Edition 2024 extension protos when CG-14 lands) pass unmodified.
Unknown extensions round-trip; registry lookup is O(1).

tasks.title: Implement maps and repeated fields with upb semantics
tasks.deliverable: Implement arena-backed arrays and hash maps with upb-compatible insert/get/remove/iterate/clear semantics, map-of-message adoption and fuse behavior.
accept: accessors_map_test, accessors_repeated_test and proto_macro_test pass unmodified; no quadratic counting remains.
Map-heavy corpus cells improve on dev-loop evidence.

tasks.title: Implement reflection interop, equality, debug and formats
tasks.deliverable: Replace remaining stubs: raw message view interop, message equality, debug string, JSON/text through descriptors for rust_out messages.
accept: Rerunning scripts/rust-out-abi.py (from UK-01) reports zero stub or missing entry points; the regenerated docs/evidence/rust-out-abi.json is committed.
Upstream debug and equality behaviors used by shared tests pass.

tasks.title: Run every upstream rust/test/shared suite unmodified in CI
tasks.deliverable: Run the complete pinned upstream shared suite (not the in-tree port) against the pbrs kernel, with each exclusion justified as C/C++-internal and reviewed; add a black-box subset of rust/test/upb where applicable.
accept: CI job fails on any unexpected failure; exclusion list is reviewed and shrinks to C++-only features.
Pass/fail counts are published per suite and compared with Google's rust_upb results.

tasks.title: Add a conformance testee built from official rust_out gencode
tasks.deliverable: Build a second conformance testee from protoc --rust_out kernel=upb output running on the pbrs kernel and run the pinned v35.1 runner (binary, JSON, text; required and recommended).
accept: Zero unexpected failures with no skip list, matching or beating rust_upb's own failure list.
CI runs both testees (plugin and rust_out) on every relevant change.

tasks.title: Beat upb on Google's own messages
tasks.deliverable: Benchmark identical rust_out gencode linked to the pbrs kernel versus the C upb kernel on TestAllTypes, google_message1/2, OTLP and Envoy corpora for encode, decode, parse-and-touch, size, merge and retained memory.
accept: Dev-loop evidence shows pbrs kernel wins or ties every primary cell; any loss has a filed follow-up card.
Claim-grade confirmation is deferred to SB-15; no universal claim.

tasks.title: Make pbrs a [patch] drop-in for google-protobuf and legacy protobuf 4.x
tasks.deliverable: Provide unpublished facades exposing the google-protobuf 0.36.x public API (and the superseded protobuf 4.x API that grpc 0.9 still uses) over the pbrs kernel so a workspace can switch with `[patch.crates-io]`; prove it with an unmodified Google grpc (grpc-protobuf) helloworld and with protobuf's own Rust examples.
accept: An unmodified Google grpc helloworld and an unmodified downstream workspace using google-protobuf (build scripts, crate features and generated code untouched) build and pass their tests with the patch and no C compiler on PATH, for every supported release pin (current 0.36.x and legacy 4.35.1).
The facades never publish under Google's crate names; naming for any published facade is a maintainer decision.

tasks.title: Differential-fuzz the kernel against upb C
tasks.deliverable: Add cargo-fuzz targets decoding and re-encoding the same bytes through the pbrs kernel and upb C (test-only harness), comparing results, errors and unknown fields; retain corpora and minimized crashes.
accept: At least 24 CPU-hours per major target with no unexplained divergence before UK-13 or UK-16 claims.
Harness never links C into shipping crates.

tasks.title: Prepare the upstream engagement packet
tasks.deliverable: Assemble a design doc and evidence bundle aimed at Google's review bar: kernel design, unmodified shared-test and conformance results, fuzz hours and findings, unsafe inventory, benchmark results on their messages, maintenance plan. Opening an upstream discussion is an operator action requiring explicit approval.
accept: Packet links only reproducible, committed evidence.
No external post is made without the maintainer's explicit approval.

tasks.title: Study a C ABI for non-Rust upb consumers
tasks.deliverable: Feasibility study (stretch): export a subset of upb's public C API (message, decode/encode, reflection defs) from the Rust kernel so Python/Ruby/PHP upb bindings could link it; identify ABI-stability, allocator and exception-safety constraints.
accept: Study lists the minimal symbol set, blocking gaps and an effort estimate; no code merged without approval.

tasks.title: Converge plugin and official paths on shared primitives
tasks.deliverable: Decide whether plugin gencode should target the UK tables/decoder (smaller code, one engine) while keeping its struct API, and which primitives (varint, UTF-8, packed, unknown fields) both paths must share now.
accept: Decision record with measured trade-offs from PK-07 and UK-13; shared primitives extracted with no regression.

tasks.title: Quantify h2 costs and decide go/no-go on a custom engine
tasks.deliverable: Measure what the h2 crate costs pbrs-grpc: mutex contention on the per-connection stream store and frame queue, wakeups per RPC, frame copies, allocations, and multi-core scaling with many streams per connection, on client and server, for small unary, streaming and large payloads. Compare with the best non-Rust transports in SB-11.
accept: Report attributes a share of CPU per RPC to h2 internals versus pbrs-grpc code, with flamegraphs and lock-contention data.

Go/no-go criterion: proceed with H2-04+ only if the modeled achievable gain on primary C/D cells is at least 15% or h2 blocks a required multi-core design; otherwise pivot to upstream h2 contributions.

tasks.title: Introduce an internal HTTP/2 transport seam
tasks.deliverable: Define crate-private traits for connection handshake, stream open/accept, send headers/data/trailers, receive, flow-control release and reset, and route all current h2 calls through an h2-backed implementation. No behavior change.
accept: All native suites, interop and hostile tests pass unchanged; dev-loop cells regress by no more than 1%.
No h2 type appears outside the backend module after the change.
tasks.notes: Valuable even if H2-01 says no-go: it isolates h2 for upstream work and enables test doubles.

tasks.title: Design the gRPC-specialized sans-IO HTTP/2 engine
tasks.deliverable: Design pbrs-h2: sans-IO connection state machine owned by one task, frame codec, HPACK with gRPC header templates, stream table without locks, connection and stream flow control with BDP estimation, SETTINGS/PING/GOAWAY/RST/CONTINUATION handling, all security limits (rapid reset, CONTINUATION flood, ping/settings flood, header list size, empty-frame abuse), write scheduling with vectored IO, and IO adapters (Tokio first, io_uring later).
accept: Design maps every RFC 9113/7541 MUST to a module and test, and every existing hostile-peer defense to its new location.
Declares performance targets per scoreboard cell and a crate-placement decision for the maintainer.

tasks.title: Create pbrs-h2 and implement the frame codec
tasks.deliverable: Create the pbrs-h2 crate (placement per H2-03) and implement zero-copy parse/serialize for every RFC 9113 frame type with length, padding and flag validation.
accept: Unit tests cover every frame type and malformed-length/padding case with the RFC error code.
Structure-aware fuzzing for 1 CPU-hour finds no panic or divergence from h2's frame decoder.

tasks.title: Implement the sans-IO stream state machine
tasks.deliverable: Implement stream lifecycle, SETTINGS negotiation, PING, GOAWAY and RST_STREAM semantics as a deterministic state machine fed with bytes and time, producing frames to write and events to deliver. Flow control and security limits follow in H2-05b/c.
accept: Deterministic tests cover every stream-state transition and error code in RFC 9113 section 5.
No stream state leaks after reset or GOAWAY (property test).

tasks.title: Implement the single-owner Tokio driver
tasks.deliverable: Drive the state machine from one task per connection that owns the socket, delivering stream events through lightweight per-stream wakers and accepting outbound work without a connection-wide mutex; plug it into the H2-02 seam behind a feature flag.
accept: All native suites, interop (Go, C++, tonic peers) and hostile tests pass on the new backend.
Dev-loop shows fewer instructions and allocations per unary RPC than the h2 backend on client and server.

tasks.title: Run h2spec and RFC conformance in CI
tasks.deliverable: Run h2spec (pinned release, test tool only) against the pbrs-h2 server and a client conformance suite against pbrs-h2 client; wire into CI.
accept: h2spec passes every applicable case; any skipped case has a documented reason.
CI fails on regression.

tasks.title: Pass official gRPC HTTP/2 negative interop on the new engine
tasks.deliverable: Run the official http2 interop cases (goaway, rst_after_header, rst_during_data, rst_after_data, ping, max_streams, data_frame_padding, no_df_padding_sanity_test) and server framing/TLS probes against the pbrs-h2 backend.
accept: Every case that passes on the h2 backend passes on pbrs-h2; results are recorded in the case registry.
Hostile-peer suite passes unchanged.

tasks.title: Differential and structure-aware fuzzing of the engine
tasks.deliverable: Fuzz pbrs-h2 against h2 as peer with random frame sequences and time, and fuzz the frame/HPACK parsers structure-aware; retain corpora.
accept: Targets build and an initial 1 CPU-hour per target runs clean; the 24 CPU-hour campaign on the candidate SHA belongs to H2-15.
Every crash becomes a regression test.

tasks.title: Pre-encode gRPC headers from codegen
tasks.deliverable: Emit per-method static header blocks (:path, content-type, te, grpc-encoding) pre-encoded for HPACK from codegen, precompute static response headers and trailers-only responses, and write prefix plus DATA header in one buffer.
accept: Wire bytes remain valid HPACK against h2, grpc-go and C++ peers (interop).
Dev-loop instructions per small unary fall on client and server.

tasks.title: Implement the write scheduler and flush policy
tasks.deliverable: Round-robin streams with a byte quantum, coalesce frames into vectored writes, flush at the end of each read burst or when the queue drains (never waiting on a timer), and evaluate TCP_QUICKACK/corking and SO_BUSY_POLL options.
accept: Mixed bulk-plus-unary fairness cell keeps small-RPC p99 within budget while bulk throughput improves.
Syscalls per RPC fall on dev-loop evidence.

tasks.title: Implement BDP-driven flow control
tasks.deliverable: Estimate bandwidth-delay product with PING samples (as grpc-go does) and grow windows dynamically within configured budgets; avoid WINDOW_UPDATE storms.
accept: Large-stream throughput over emulated 1 ms and 10 ms RTT beats static windows without exceeding memory budgets.
Resource-budget tests remain green.

tasks.title: Shrink per-connection and per-stream memory
tasks.deliverable: Pool read/write buffers, size stream state compactly, and release idle connection buffers, targeting the best measured RSS per idle connection and per active stream in SB-12.
accept: SB-12 memory cells beat the h2 backend and tie or beat grpc-go.
No buffer pool grows without bound (soak test).

tasks.title: Decide the default HTTP/2 backend
tasks.deliverable: Switch the default to pbrs-h2 only when correctness gates (h2spec, interop, hostile, fuzz hours, soak) pass and the scoreboard shows wins on primary client and server cells; keep the h2 backend as a fallback feature for at least two releases.
accept: Decision record links every gate result and scoreboard cell; rollback is a feature flag.
Release notes describe the change and fallback.

tasks.title: Introduce a minimal runtime seam
tasks.deliverable: Isolate spawn, timers and socket IO behind crate-private traits that compile to direct Tokio calls, so alternative runtimes can be tested without touching protocol code.
accept: Zero measurable dev-loop regression on Tokio; no public API change.
A test-only runtime double exercises timeouts deterministically.

tasks.title: Offer thread-per-core server and client modes
tasks.deliverable: Add an opt-in mode with N current-thread runtimes pinned to cores, SO_REUSEPORT-sharded listeners, per-core connection ownership and per-core client pools, avoiding cross-core synchronization on the hot path.
accept: Multi-core scaling efficiency (1 to 16 cores) beats the work-stealing mode and the best SB-11 peer on primary server cells.
Graceful shutdown, drain and limits behave identically to the default mode.

tasks.title: Experiment with an io_uring backend
tasks.deliverable: Prototype a Linux io_uring IO adapter for the pbrs-h2 driver using a reviewed crate (dependency review required) and measure syscalls, CPU per RPC and tail latency against epoll.
accept: Decision record adopts or rejects on SB-11 evidence; rejection is valid.
If adopted, it is opt-in, Linux-only, and passes the full native suite.

tasks.title: Benchmark TLS providers and handshake paths
tasks.deliverable: Measure rustls with graviola, ring and aws-lc-rs (the last is not pure Rust and is benchmark-only) for handshake rate, resumption, bulk throughput and CPU per RPC; implement session resumption and ticket reuse in the client and server.
accept: Pure-Rust default is chosen on evidence; the non-pure option is documented as an explicit opt-in if ever offered.
TLS cells in SB-11/SB-12 improve with resumption; TLS tests pass.

tasks.title: Experiment with kernel TLS offload
tasks.deliverable: Prototype Linux kTLS for established rustls sessions on bulk streams and measure CPU per byte; keep it opt-in.
accept: Decision record with evidence; security review of key handling before any merge.

tasks.title: Upgrade compression: zlib-rs backend and zstd decision
tasks.deliverable: Switch gzip/deflate to the fastest reviewed pure-Rust backend (evaluate flate2's zlib-rs backend versus miniz_oxide), add deflate if absent, and decide on zstd support from available pure-Rust encoders/decoders.
accept: Compression interop (gzip cases with Go and C++) passes; no C in the graph (dep-audit).
Compressed-payload cells improve on dev-loop evidence; zstd decision recorded.

tasks.title: Add buffer pools and allocator guidance
tasks.deliverable: Pool encode/decode BytesMut buffers per connection where profiles show allocator pressure, and publish measured guidance for system, mimalloc and jemalloc allocators.
accept: Allocations per RPC fall on dev-loop evidence; pools are bounded and covered by resource-budget tests.
Guidance lists measured deltas per allocator on SB-11 cells.

tasks.title: Isolate the native client's limiting costs
tasks.deliverable: Profile the native client against fixed independent servers (C++ and Go) for unary and each streaming shape, across connections, TLS and offered load, attributing serialization, copies, header construction, boxed futures, watch channels, pool locking, h2 sender contention, wakeups and TLS.
accept: Server headroom is verified for every cell; uses dev-loop tooling with the existing pinned Go/C++ peers (scripts/rpc-bench-matrix.py) and adopts SB-11 cells once they exist.
CL-02 through CL-06 each receive a hypothesis with baseline artifacts; disproved hypotheses re-scope their cards.

tasks.title: Specialize the unary call path
tasks.deliverable: Remove per-call boxed futures, the watch cancellation channel and Channel clones from unary calls where cancellation can be expressed by drop; stop copying the path into successful response context.
accept: Cancellation, deadline, drop and retry-safety tests pass unchanged.
Allocations and instructions per unary RPC fall on dev-loop evidence; C1/C2 cells improve.

tasks.title: Precompute request headers and timeout encoding
tasks.deliverable: Build per-channel/per-method header templates (authority, scheme, content-type, te, user-agent, path) once, format grpc-timeout without temporary Strings, and avoid per-call Uri construction.
accept: Wire headers are byte-identical except where intended; interop passes.
Instructions per small unary fall on dev-loop evidence.

tasks.title: Pick connections without locks and respect peer stream limits
tasks.deliverable: Replace the Tokio Mutex slot pick with a lock-free ready-connection pick, choose least-loaded connections, and grow the pool when the peer lowers MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS (A105).
accept: Pool behavior under churn, dead slots and redial is unchanged in tests; A105 behavior is covered by a peer that lowers its stream cap.
C2 multi-connection cells improve and contention disappears from client profiles.

tasks.title: Remove streaming client pumps
tasks.deliverable: Write client-streaming and bidi messages directly from the caller's send path instead of a spawned pump with oneshots, preserving producer-failure and reset semantics.
accept: Streaming lifecycle, cancellation and hostile tests pass unchanged.
C3 cells improve; task spawns per bidi call fall to zero on dev-loop evidence.

tasks.title: Minimize cold start and client memory
tasks.deliverable: Reduce time-to-first-RPC (DNS, TCP, TLS, HTTP/2 preface/SETTINGS pipelining) and per-channel/per-stream memory.
accept: C6 and C7 cells improve and beat tonic; lazy-connect and wait-for-ready semantics unchanged.

tasks.title: Isolate the native server's limiting costs
tasks.deliverable: Profile the native server under a fixed independent load generator for unary and streaming shapes across cores, connections, TLS and offered load, attributing accept, per-RPC spawn, metadata/path copies, tracker construction, router boxing, encode, trailers and h2 internals.
accept: Generator headroom verified for every cell.
SV-02 through SV-07 each receive a hypothesis with baseline artifacts.

tasks.title: Remove redundant per-RPC server allocations
tasks.deliverable: Drop the throwaway ByteBudgetTracker, repeated path/authority/scheme copies, and per-RPC construction of OK trailers; share immutable connection facts by reference.
accept: Interceptor-visible context and metadata are unchanged (tests).
Allocations per unary RPC fall on dev-loop evidence; D2/D4 improve.

tasks.title: Dispatch without a spawn per RPC where safe
tasks.deliverable: Experiment with polling unary handlers on the connection task under a cooperative budget, or reusing task allocations, falling back to spawn for long-running handlers; measure head-of-line risk.
accept: Decision with evidence; if adopted, a slow handler cannot stall other streams beyond a documented budget (fairness test).
D2 improves on primary cells without p99 regression beyond 5%.

tasks.title: Generate static method routing
tasks.deliverable: Emit per-service static dispatch (match or perfect hash over full method paths) and an enum-dispatched router for multi-service servers, removing boxed futures and string hashing per call.
accept: Unknown service/method still returns UNIMPLEMENTED; reflection and health still route.
Router instructions per call fall on dev-loop evidence.

tasks.title: Use static trailers and trailers-only responses
tasks.deliverable: Precompute OK trailers and emit trailers-only responses for immediate errors (UNIMPLEMENTED, RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, deadline), matching grpc-go/C++ wire behavior.
accept: Interop and status tests pass with all peers; error paths allocate less.

tasks.title: Optimize bounded streaming batches and fairness
tasks.deliverable: Tune OutBatch size/flush policy and the yield heuristic by measurement with explicit byte/time bounds, preserving immediate progress for ping-pong streams.
accept: D3 improves without worsening mixed unary p99 beyond budget; backpressure, cancellation and trailers correct under hostile fixtures.

tasks.title: Scale accepts and cut per-connection server memory
tasks.deliverable: Add optional SO_REUSEPORT multi-acceptor listeners and accept batching, and shrink idle-connection state.
accept: D5/D6 cells improve; connection caps and handshake timeouts behave as before.

tasks.title: Decide the better-tonic product shape and names
tasks.deliverable: Decide which adoption paths ship and under what names: (a) tonic-shaped API mode for native stubs, (b) tower server/client integration, (c) prost-message support over the native transport, (d) the existing protobuf-tonic adapter. Resolve the open pbrs-tonic naming question as part of it.
accept: Decision record covers crate names, features, semver/release impact and the migration story for tonic+prost, tonic+pbrs and grpc-rust users.
Maintainer approval recorded before TC-02 through TC-06.

tasks.title: Abstract the native codec over message types
tasks.deliverable: Introduce a codec trait in pbrs-grpc (pbrs messages by default) so generated or hand-written services can use other message types without transport changes; keep pbrs fast paths (direct encode into frame, Bytes parse).
accept: pbrs dev-loop cells unchanged within 1%; a test codec proves foreign types work for all four shapes.

tasks.title: Serve prost messages over the native transport
tasks.deliverable: Add an optional prost codec and a service generator that consumes prost-build message output and emits native pbrs-grpc stubs, so tonic+prost users adopt the faster transport without changing message types.
accept: tonic's routeguide and helloworld protos build with prost messages and native stubs; interop with tonic peers passes.
Client and server C/D cells with prost messages still beat tonic on SB-11 dev-loop evidence.

tasks.title: Expose native services as tower services
tasks.deliverable: Provide an optional adapter so a pbrs-grpc Router is a tower::Service<http::Request<B>> that can be mounted in axum/hyper alongside REST routes, and allow tower layers around handlers.
accept: An example co-hosts gRPC and axum on one port; health/reflection work through the adapter.
The adapter is feature-gated; the default dependency graph is unchanged.

tasks.title: Support tower middleware on the client
tasks.deliverable: Allow tower layers (timeouts, concurrency limit, load shed, tracing) around the native Channel behind a feature, without putting a buffer in the default path.
accept: Default client path allocations unchanged; layered path documented with measured overhead.

tasks.title: Offer a tonic-shaped API mode and migration kit
tasks.deliverable: Add a codegen mode whose client/server signatures mirror tonic (Request/Response/Status/Streaming, async trait style, stream-accepting client methods) over the native transport, plus a migration guide with a mechanical rewrite table.
accept: Self-contained compile fixtures port tonic's helloworld and routeguide handlers into the mode, changing only imports and builder setup, and pass all four RPC shapes.
Native mode remains the default and unchanged.

tasks.title: Port tonic's examples and publish migration diffs
tasks.deliverable: Port tonic's public examples (helloworld, routeguide, streaming, interceptor, health, reflection, TLS, UDS, compression) to each adoption path and publish line-diff statistics and any blockers.
accept: Each example runs and interoperates with its original tonic counterpart.
Diff statistics and blockers are published in the migration guide.

tasks.title: Audit tonic feature parity and file gap cards
tasks.deliverable: Build a feature matrix versus tonic (TLS options, UDS, interceptors, compression, timeouts, keepalive, concurrency/load-shed, connect info, extensions, gRPC-Web) from TC-07's migration blockers, and add one bounded card per gap that blocks a real migration.
accept: Matrix published in the comparison guide with status per feature and linked tests.
Every blocking gap has a new card in tasks.json with scope and acceptance; no parity code is written under this card.

tasks.title: Decide gRPC-Web and Connect protocol scope
tasks.deliverable: Decide whether to support gRPC-Web (tonic-web parity) and the Connect protocol natively, with an independent peer for interop.
accept: Decision record with demand, design sketch and test peer; implementation cards added if approved.

tasks.title: Speed up the protobuf-tonic adapter
tasks.deliverable: Use PK-09's Bytes parse in the adapter decoder (copy_to_bytes then parse_bytes) so large fields share tonic's buffer, and verify encode writes directly into EncodeBuf.
accept: Adapter tests pass; large-payload tonic+pbrs cells beat tonic+prost with Bytes fields on SB-13 evidence.

tasks.title: Add a pbrs-grpc entry to the public grpc_bench harness
tasks.deliverable: Add a pbrs-grpc server (multi-thread and single-thread variants) to a local checkout of LesnyRumcajs/grpc_bench at a pinned commit and run its standard 1/2/4-CPU scenarios beside the tonic, Thruster, grpc-go, grpc-java, Vert.x, ASP.NET and C++ entries. Submitting upstream is an operator action requiring approval.
accept: Local runs reproduce the harness's published methodology (plaintext unary, 50 connections, 1,000 concurrent calls, warmup and duration) and record host details; results are labeled diagnostic reproduction, and claims use SB-21 variants.
Reference points dated 2026-04-22 (4-CPU leader 149,776 req/s; 1-CPU leader 102,754 req/s) are re-measured on the same host, never compared across hosts.
No upstream PR is opened without explicit approval.

tasks.title: Design the channel architecture
tasks.deliverable: Design the client channel model on gRPC's resolver -> service config -> LB policy tree -> subchannel -> picker architecture, with connectivity states, plugin registries for resolvers and LB policies, and hard performance rules: per-call pick is O(1), lock-free and allocation-free; policy updates never block RPCs.
accept: Design maps A5, A10, A17, A21, A24, A61, A62, A105 and A113 behavior to components and tests, and explains how xDS policies (A27, A56, A50, A42, A48, A58) plug in later.
Existing host:port Channel behavior is preserved as the default passthrough path; the design names the post-MX-02 client submodules each component lands in.
Maintainer approval before CH-02+ (supersedes the narrower FL-01 design scope).

tasks.title: Add target URI schemes and a resolver registry
tasks.deliverable: Implement dns:///, unix:, unix-abstract:, ipv4:, ipv6: and passthrough: targets with a resolver registry; IP literals and localhost skip DNS TXT lookup (A10).
accept: Existing host:port targets behave exactly as before; each scheme has tests including invalid inputs.
Resolver updates are delivered without blocking RPC picks.

tasks.title: Deliver service config through resolvers and select LB policies
tasks.deliverable: Wire the service-config parser to resolver-delivered configs (A2 DNS TXT, with A21 error handling and fallback to last good config) and implement loadBalancingConfig selection (A24) through the LB registry.
accept: Invalid configs follow A21 (keep previous good config; fail channel only when none); tests cover each rule.
Builds on the service-config parser landed by MX-00; no duplicate parser.

tasks.title: Race dual-stack connections and shuffle weighted addresses in pick_first
tasks.deliverable: Implement A61 address interleaving and connection racing, and A113 weighted shuffling, inside pick_first subchannel connection attempts.
accept: IPv4-only, IPv6-only and broken-IPv6 fixtures connect within the documented delay; no duplicate established connections leak.

tasks.title: Integrate client-side health checking with load balancing
tasks.deliverable: Use grpc.health.v1 Watch per subchannel (A17) to gate readiness in round_robin and other policies when configured.
accept: Unhealthy backends stop receiving new RPCs within one Watch update; health-service absence follows A17 rules.

tasks.title: Implement ORCA and weighted round robin
tasks.deliverable: Implement ORCA per-call and out-of-band load reports (A51) on server and client, and weighted_round_robin (A58, A114) using them, with A78 metrics hooks.
accept: Interop with a pinned grpc-go ORCA peer; WRR weights converge in a multi-backend fixture.
Picker stays lock-free and allocation-free within the CH-10 budget (qualified in CH-11).

tasks.title: Implement ring hash, least request and subsetting
tasks.deliverable: Implement ring_hash (A42, A76), least_request (A48) and random/rendezvous subsetting (A68) as standalone policies usable with and without xDS.
accept: Distribution tests match the gRFC expectations within tolerance; picks stay within the CH-10 budget.

tasks.title: Implement priority and outlier detection policies
tasks.deliverable: Implement priority (A56, A115) and outlier_detection (A50, A91) LB policies with bounded state.
accept: Failover and ejection timelines match the gRFCs under fake clocks; metrics hooks present.

tasks.title: Add HTTP CONNECT proxy, TCP user timeout and binary-metadata interop
tasks.deliverable: Implement A1 HTTP CONNECT (HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY), A18 TCP_USER_TIMEOUT on Linux, and interop-verified true binary metadata (G1).
accept: Proxy tunneling works through a test proxy with TLS end-to-end; A18 option applied and tested on Linux.
Binary metadata round-trips with Go and C++ peers.

tasks.title: Build the picker-cost harness and budget
tasks.deliverable: Add dev-loop cells that measure pick cost, allocations and lock acquisitions for any LB policy, with a recorded instruction budget; policies adopt it as they land and CH-11 qualifies all of them.
accept: The harness measures the passthrough picker today and fails the perf lane if a pick allocates, locks or exceeds the budget.

tasks.title: Decide build versus reuse for xDS machinery
tasks.deliverable: Evaluate grpc/grpc-rust's xds-client and tonic-xds alphas, junction-labs xds-api bindings and an in-repo implementation against pbrs-grpc's pure-Rust, performance and API constraints; decide what to reuse, contribute to, or build.
accept: Decision covers dependency graph (tonic/prost pulls), licensing, API fit with CH-01, maintenance and upstream collaboration.
Maintainer approval recorded; supersedes the scope portion of EX-07.

tasks.title: Generate xDS protos and stand up a local control-plane fixture
